title: Seller's Property Condition Disclosure
description: New Hampshire requires sellers of residential real estate to complete a Seller's Property Condition Disclosure form covering structural, mechanical, environmental, and other known conditions of the property. Must be delivered to buyer before or at the time the purchase and sale agreement is signed.

required_actions.note: Seller must disclose all known material defects. Failure to disclose may result in liability for damages.

title: Agency Disclosure and Consent
description: New Hampshire licensees must disclose their agency relationship in writing at the first personal meeting with a prospective buyer or seller. Dual agency is permitted only with written informed consent of all parties. The disclosure must explain the duties owed under each type of relationship.

title: Radon Gas Disclosure
description: New Hampshire requires sellers to disclose known radon gas conditions affecting the property. The seller's disclosure form includes specific questions about radon testing results and any mitigation systems installed. New Hampshire has significant radon risk areas, and EPA recommends testing in all homes.

required_actions.note: Radon section on NH-SPCDS. Seller must disclose known radon test results and any mitigation.
Buyer strongly advised to conduct independent radon test during inspection period.

title: Closing Type — Attorney State
description: New Hampshire is an attorney-closing state. While not strictly mandated by statute, custom and practice strongly favor attorney involvement in residential real estate transactions. Title examination is typically performed by an attorney, and most lenders require attorney certification of title.

required_actions.note: Attorney involvement strongly recommended. Title examination typically performed by licensed attorney.

title: Private Well Water Testing and Disclosure
description: For properties served by private wells, New Hampshire requires water quality testing and disclosure. The seller must provide the buyer with information about the water supply, including known contamination issues. FHA and VA loans require well testing.

required_actions.note: Test for bacteria, nitrate, fluoride, arsenic, radon in water, and other contaminants per NHDES standards.
